property_summary: After calling newEmergencyOracle with a specific admin, the reference contract sets the owner of the new oracle to msg.sender, while the bug sets it to address(0), making owner() return zero address in the buggy version.

Calling newEmergencyOracle with an admin sets the new oracle's owner to msg.sender in P, but to address(0) in M; we get the new oracle address from the event, then check that the owner is not address(0) for P and is address(0) for M.
After calling newEmergencyOracle with an admin, the reference sets the new oracle's owner to msg.sender, while the bug sets it to address(0); we assert that the owner is not address(0).

After calling newEmergencyOracle with 'test', the new oracle's turnOn is true in the reference but false in the bug because the bug's oracle is owned by address(0) and admin attempts to turn it on fail.

After calling newEmergencyOracle('test') as an admin, the reference sets the owner of the new oracle to msg.sender, while the bug sets it to address(0); we read the new oracle's owner via a getter on the deployed EmergencyOracle to show the divergence.

After calling newEmergencyOracle with an admin caller, the reference contract emits an event with the correct owner (msg.sender) while the buggy contract uses address(1), causing the getter for the event owner to differ when reading the event log.
Calling newEmergencyOracle with an admin claims the new oracle owner is msg.sender in P, but in M it is address(1), so after deploying we can read the new oracle's owner() and it differs.
When an admin calls newEmergencyOracle, the deployed EmergencyOracle has owner() == admin in P but owner() == address(1) in M.
After an admin calls newEmergencyOracle, the deployed EmergencyOracle's owner() returns the admin in P but returns address(1) in M.
When an admin (address(0xdead)) calls newEmergencyOracle, the reference contract deploys an EmergencyOracle whose owner() returns address(0xdead), while the buggy version returns address(1).

When a non-admin user calls newEmergencyOracle, on reference C it reverts due to onlyAdmin modifier, while on buggy M it succeeds and emits NewEmergencyOracle, allowing any user to deploy an EmergencyOracle.
After calling newEmergencyOracle as admin, the reference emits an event with the admin's address as first parameter, while the buggy version emits with address(0).
After calling newEmergencyOracle as admin, the reference emits an event with the admin's address as first parameter, while the buggy version emits with address(0).

When admin calls newEmergencyOracle with description 'test', the newly created EmergencyOracle's owner is the admin in the reference (due to emit NewEmergencyOracle(msg.sender, newOracle)), but in the buggy version the owner is address(0) (due to emit NewEmergencyOracle(address(0), newOracle)), causing a revert when the admin calls turnOffOracle on the new oracle.

After admin calls newEmergencyOracle, the reference creates an EmergencyOracle whose owner is msg.sender (the admin), while the buggy version creates one whose owner is address(0), causing the admin to be unable to call turnOffOracle on the new oracle (revert).

When admin calls newEmergencyOracle with description 'test', the reference creates an EmergencyOracle whose owner is the admin (msg.sender), while the buggy version creates one whose owner is address(0), so the admin can call turnOn via the new EmergencyOracle in the reference, but the call reverts in the buggy version because onlyOwner modifier fails.

When msg.sender is not an admin and also not the owner passed to EmergencyOracle, reference C sets the oracle owner to msg.sender (who is admin) and emits NewEmergencyOracle(msg.sender, ...), but mutant M sets the oracle owner to address(this) (the contract C), so after deployment, the owner() of the new oracle differs (reference owner == admin address, mutant owner == C contract address). In particular, if the admin calls newEmergencyOracle, the reference makes the admin the owner, allowing admin to call setAssetPrice; the mutant makes C the owner, so setAssetPrice called by admin reverts.

A non-admin calls newEmergencyOracle, which reverts in reference C due to onlyAdmin modifier, but in mutant M the onlyAdmin check passes mistakenly because the bug modifies the modifier logic to allow non-admin calls, so the reference reverts and the mutant does not.

When an admin calls newEmergencyOracle, the reference sets the new EmergencyOracle's owner to msg.sender (the admin), while the mutant sets it to address(this) (the contract C). After deployment, calling setAssetPrice on the new oracle from the admin address succeeds in the reference but reverts in the mutant.

An admin calls newEmergencyOracle with a specific description; the reference stores the admin as the EmergencyOracle owner (so admin can setAssetPrice), but the mutant stores address(this) as owner, causing setAssetPrice from admin to revert.

An admin calls newEmergencyOracle; in the reference, the admin is set as the EmergencyOracle owner (so admin can call setAssetPrice without revert), but in the mutant, address(this) (the C contract) is the owner, so admin's setAssetPrice call reverts.
